## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** Ongoing / unresolved as of the last log entry (`2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z`) — pool still saturated, wait queue climbing (13 → 74+), no recovery observed.

**Root cause:**
Deploy `dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak, "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation") applied config generation 119 at `02:13:41.234Z`, flipping `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true`. This changed connection acquisition to per-request instead of shared/pooled, and the fixed pool (size 20) exhausted almost immediately. Every 503 is paired with `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)` — not a downstream service failure (billing-svc, orders-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc all affected equally across `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/orders`).

**Impact window:**
- First 503: `2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z` (~33s after config applied; first warning sign was a `WARN pool acquire slow` at `02:14:14.920Z`)
- Still failing at end of available logs: `03:59:27.974Z` (1h45m+ and counting)
- Scope: gateway only. Confirmed via `worker.log` — zero errors, healthy pool stats (`in_use=1`, `waiting=0`) throughout the same window, jobs completing normally. No DB or worker impact.

**Rollback target:**
`dep-4471` — gateway deploy, `2026-03-14T02:12:00Z`–`02:14:00Z`, author a.novak. Revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false` (or raise pool size if per-request is intentionally needed) and redeploy.

**Note:** No other deploy in the window is implicated — `dep-4472` (billing-svc, 02:41) and `dep-4473` (catalog-svc, 03:20) came after the incident started and don't correlate with the error pattern.
